Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: Kolmogorov-Chapman Maps: Trajectory-Free Learning for Simulating Molecular Dynamics
items.summary: Stochastic differential equations (SDEs) describe stochastic processes across a wide range of scientific domains, including physics, biology, and finance. Although individual numerical integration steps are inexpensive, observing meaningful events or transitions can require millions of sequential steps, resulting in substantial wall-clock simulation time and poor hardware utilization. Deep learning offers an alternative by amortizing many integration steps into a single neural network forward pass, potentially enabling much faster simulation. However, existing supervised approaches typically require long simulated trajectory data, which restricts their applicability. In this work, we introduce Kolmogorov-Chapman Maps (KC-Maps), a method for learning the transition kernel of an SDE that relies only on the trajectory-free marginal samples together with the known drift and diffusion coefficients. Given an initial time and state of a process, KC-Maps models its distribution integrated to any given time, corresponding to the weak solution of the SDE. To recover the correct dynamics, KC-Maps satisfies two key properties: (i) it satisfies the boundary conditions, which we incorporate directly into the neural network architecture, and (ii) it respects the Kolmogorov--Chapman equation, which provides an efficient training objective. We empirically demonstrate that KC-Maps learns to integrate the dynamics of peptide molecular systems and outperforms classical molecular dynamics in terms of GPU-hours.

items.title: What kills $v$-prediction? A Patch-wise PCA Perspective on Pixel-Space Flow Matching
items.summary: Latent Diffusion Models dominate generative modeling but face two-stage training complexity and the inherent reconstruction limits of pre-trained autoencoders. Pixel-space Flow Matching offers a simplified end-to-end alternative yet often encounters training difficulties when using the standard $v$-prediction objective. Recent research attributes this difficulty to the off-manifold nature of noised targets, motivating a shift toward $x$-prediction. In this paper, we investigate this explanation through patch-wise Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and identify a bandwidth bottleneck. The velocity in minor components is largely determined by the raw noisy input, requiring deep backbones to preserve information that competes with principal-component modeling. Through controlled experiments and representation analysis, we further examine why $x$-prediction remains effective: its parameterization provides a raw-input bypass, while its learned input representation can spontaneously concentrate on principal directions. Under low-rank observations, our analysis of the induced flow characterizes $x$-prediction as an implicit conditional-mean decoder, reconstructing discarded components from the retained information. These observations motivate the Raw-injected Transformer (RiT), which combines a lightweight raw-conditioned decoder with an output-side shortcut to separate semantic modeling from raw-state propagation. Our method restores effective $v$-prediction and achieves competitive performance on ImageNet $256\times256$, providing a perspective on the interaction between prediction objectives and architectural bandwidth.

items.title: Learning Heterogeneous Tactile Representation for General Dexterous Manipulation
items.summary: Tactile sensing is an indispensable modality for contact-rich dexterous manipulation, a capability that hints at the ultimate frontiers of embodied intelligence. However, commercially available tactile sensors are still at a relatively early stage of development, with each type of sensor offering irreplaceable strengths alongside its own drawbacks. A key challenge is thus to free tactile understanding from sensor-specific physics, so that embodied models can effectively leverage heterogeneous tactile data. To this end, we develop LingBot-Touch, a tactile foundation model characterized by the following properties. (i) Our model yields a unified representation across different tactile sensors (i.e., piezoresistive, magnetic, and visuotactile sensors), and is easily extensible to new sensor types. (ii) The resulting tactile tokens are plug-and-play: they can be seamlessly integrated into policy models across paradigms, from diffusion policy to vision-language-action (VLA) models such as $π_{0.5}$ and LingBot-VLA, consistently enhancing manipulation dexterity. (iii) Extensive experiments, spanning simulation and real-robot deployments across multiple hardware platforms, demonstrate that our tactile representation substantially benefits complex manipulation tasks while maintaining strong computational efficiency. We believe the findings in this work demonstrate the potential of leveraging cross-sensor data to scale tactile learning, and offer encouraging insights for the design of future hardware and embodied models.

items.summary:

illia.polosukhin@gmail.com
Abstract
The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or
convolutional neural networks that include an encoder and a decoder. The best
performing models also connect the encoder and decoder through an attention
mechanism. We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer,
based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions
entirely. Experiments on two machine translation tasks show these models to
be superior in quality while being more parallelizable and requiring significantly
less time to train. Our model achieves 28.4 BLEU on the WMT 2014 English-
to-German translation task, improving over the existing best results, including
ensembles, by over 2 BLEU. On the WMT 2014 English-to-French translation task,
our model establishes a new single-model state-of-the-art BLEU score of 41.8 after
training for 3.5 days on eight GPUs, a small fraction of the training costs of the
best models from the literature. We show that the Transformer generalizes well to
other tasks by applying it successfully to English constituency parsing both with
large and limited training data.
∗Equal contribution. Listing order is random. Jakob proposed replacing RNNs with self-attention and started
the effort to evaluate this idea. Ashish, with Illia, designed and implemented the first Transformer models and
has been crucially involved in every aspect of this work. Noam proposed scaled dot-product attention, multi-head
attention and the parameter-free position representation and became the other person involved in nearly every
detail. Niki designed, implemented, tuned and evaluated countless model variants in our original codebase and
tensor2tensor. Llion also experimented with novel model variants, was responsible for our initial codebase, and
efficient inference and visualizations. Lukasz and Aidan spent countless long days designing various parts of and
implementing tensor2tensor, replacing our earlier codebase, greatly improving results and massively accelerating
our research.
†Work performed while at Google Brain.
‡Work performed while at Google Research.
31st Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NIPS 2017), Long Beach, CA, USA.
arXiv:1706.03762v7  [cs.CL]  2 Aug 2023

1 Introduction
Recurrent neural networks, long short-term memory [13] and gated recurrent [7] neural networks
in particular, have been firmly established as state of the art approaches in sequence modeling and
transduction problems such as language modeling and machine translation [ 35, 2, 5]. Numerous
efforts have since continued to push the boundaries of recurrent language models and encoder-decoder
architectures [38, 24, 15].
Recurrent models typically factor computation along the symbol positions of the input and output
sequences. Aligning the positions to steps in computation time, they generate a sequence of hidden
states ht, as a function of the previous hidden state ht−1 and the input for position t. This inherently
sequential nature precludes parallelization within training examples, which becomes critical at longer
sequence lengths, as memory constraints limit batching across examples. Recent work has achieved
significant improvements in computational efficiency through factorization tricks [21] and conditional
computation [32], while also improving model performance in case of the latter. The fundamental
constraint of sequential computation, however, remains.
Attention mechanisms have become an integral part of compelling sequence modeling and transduc-
tion models in various tasks, allowing modeling of dependencies without regard to their distance in
the input or output sequences [2, 19]. In all but a few cases [27], however, such attention mechanisms
are used in conjunction with a recurrent network.
In this work we propose the Transformer, a model architecture eschewing recurrence and instead
relying entirely on an attention mechanism to draw global dependencies between input and output.
The Transformer allows for significantly more parallelization and can reach a new state of the art in
translation quality after being trained for as little as twelve hours on eight P100 GPUs.
2 Background
The goal of reducing sequential computation also forms the foundation of the Extended Neural GPU
[16], ByteNet [18] and ConvS2S [9], all of which use convolutional neural networks as basic building
block, computing hidden representations in parallel for all input and output positions. In these models,
the number of operations required to relate signals from two arbitrary input or output positions grows
in the distance between positions, linearly for ConvS2S and logarithmically for ByteNet. This makes
it more difficult to learn dependencies between distant positions [ 12]. In the Transformer this is
reduced to a constant number of operations, albeit at the cost of reduced effective resolution due
to averaging attention-weighted positions, an effect we counteract with Multi-Head Attention as
described in section 3.2.
Self-attention, sometimes called intra-attention is an attention mechanism relating different positions
of a single sequence in order to compute a representation of the sequence. Self-attention has been
used successfully in a variety of tasks including reading comprehension, abstractive summarization,
textual entailment and learning task-independent sentence representations [4, 27, 28, 22].
End-to-end memory networks are based on a recurrent attention mechanism instead of sequence-
aligned recurrence and have been shown to perform well on simple-language question answering and
language modeling tasks [34].
To the best of our knowledge, however, the Transformer is the first transduction model relying
entirely on self-attention to compute representations of its input and output without using sequence-
aligned RNNs or convolution. In the following sections, we will describe the Transformer, motivate
self-attention and discuss its advantages over models such as [17, 18] and [9].
3 Model Architecture
Most competitive neural sequence transduction models have an encoder-decoder structure [5, 2, 35].
Here, the encoder maps an input sequence of symbol representations (x1, ..., xn) to a sequence
of continuous representations z = (z1, ..., zn). Given z, the decoder then generates an output
sequence (y1, ..., ym) of symbols one element at a time. At each step the model is auto-regressive
[10], consuming the previously generated symbols as additional input when generating the next.
2

Figure 1: The Transformer - model architecture.
The Transformer follows this overall architecture using stacked self-attention and point-wise, fully
connected layers for both the encoder and decoder, shown in the left and right halves of Figure 1,
respectively.
3.1 Encoder and Decoder Stacks
Encoder: The encoder is composed of a stack of N = 6 identical layers. Each layer has two
sub-layers. The first is a multi-head self-attention mechanism, and the second is a simple, position-
wise fully connected feed-forward network. We employ a residual connection [11] around each of
the two sub-layers, followed by layer normalization [ 1]. That is, the output of each sub-layer is
LayerNorm(x + Sublayer(x)), where Sublayer(x) is the function implemented by the sub-layer
itself. To facilitate these residual connections, all sub-layers in the model, as well as the embedding

items.title: THIS IS ACTUAL F*CKING GOLD
items.summary:
THIS IS ACTUAL F*CKING GOLD

Anthropic just shared one of the best tricks for Claude Code.

The idea: run Sonnet, Haiku and Opus 5.5 together, each one doing only the job it's best at.

Opus-level judgment on every big call, without paying Opus rates for every routine turn.

You just launch Claude Code like this:

claude --model sonnet --advisor opus

here's the split:

→ Sonnet 5.5 runs the session and writes the code
→ Haiku 5.5 explores files and docs in parallel
→ Opus 5.5 stays on call as advisor for the big calls
→ you stop spending Opus on work that doesn't need it

Opus only steps in at three moments:

→ before a plan locks
→ when the same error shows up twice
→ before calling it done

Sonnet builds. Haiku explores. Opus reviews.

JEV engineering is the same move one layer down: the forks that need no thinker (which file, which tool, retry or stop) go to JEV in milliseconds, and the big models only see the ones that split

the full tree
> Sonnet 5.5 runs the main session and edits code
> search maps the repo on Haiku 5.5
> grep finds call sites on Haiku 5.5
> docs pulls the API reference on Haiku 5.5
> Opus 5.5 on call as advisor, reads the whole transcript when consulted
> JEV routes micro-forks in milliseconds

paste the tree and this prompt into Claude Code ↓

"Rebuild my Claude Code setup around this tree:
1. Run the main session on Sonnet 5.5 with Opus 5.5 as advisor.
2. Create three read-only Haiku 5.5 subagents: search (maps the repo), grep (finds call sites), docs (pulls the API reference).
3. Add one rule to CLAUDE.md: consult the advisor before locking a plan, after the same error twice, and before calling a task done.
4. Route fast deterministic forks (tool choice, path selection, retries) through JEV.
Show me every change as a diff first. No edits until I say go."

↳ https://t.co/bsYb2K5H9G

save it, you'll use this every single day.

Riêng tại Đông Phi, vào cuối năm nay, UNHCR cảnh báo lũ lụt nghiêm trọng kết hợp với hiện tượng El Niño cực mạnh có thể khiến tới 3 triệu người phải di dời ở Somalia, Kenya, Nam Sudan và Uganda vào cuối năm nay. Một phần ba số trại tị nạn ở vùng cận Sahara chu Phi có thể phải trải qua ít nhất 100 ngày nắng nóng nguy hiểm mỗi năm [...] Thư TinHãy nhận thư tin hàng ngày của RFI: Bản tin thời sự, phóng sự, phỏng vấn, phn tích, chn dung, tạp chí

items.title: COP31 về biến đổi khí hậu khai mạc tại Thổ Nhĩ Kỳ
items.summary: COP31 khai mạc tại Thổ Nhĩ Kỳ vào ngày 9/11 với trọng tâm thúc đẩy hợp tác quốc tế và chuyển các cam kết khí hậu thành hành động thực chất.

items.title: Chủ động thích ứng, giữ nhịp sản xuất trước biến đổi khí hậu - Báo Đắk Lắk điện tử
items.summary:
Ông Nguyễn Thái Hòa, Phó Giám đốc Sở Nông nghiệp và Môi trường tỉnh cho biết, trước những diễn biến ngày càng bất thường của thời tiết, đặc biệt là nguy cơ hạn hán gia tăng khi hiện tượng El Niño được dự báo có cường độ mạnh, tỉnh đã và đang chủ động triển khai nhiều giải pháp ứng phó. Trong đó, tập trung phòng, chống thiên tai, sạt lở, hạn hán; đầu tư, nng cấp các công trình thủy lợi, hồ chứa nước, đồng thời khuyến khích nhn rộng các mô hình nông nghiệp thích ứng với biến đổi khí hậu của người [...] Đầu tư chế biến su, khai thác tối đa giá trị

Không chỉ tìm cách thích ứng với tình trạng ngập lụt, nhiều HTX còn chủ động ứng dụng công nghệ vào sản xuất, chế biến nhằm giảm áp lực từ hạn hán, tối ưu hóa nguồn tài nguyên và hạn chế những biến động của thị trường. Đy được xem là giải pháp quan trọng để nng cao giá trị nông sản, ổn định đầu ra và tăng khả năng chống chịu trước tác động của biến đổi khí hậu. [...] |  |

| Đặt bảo vệ môi trường và ứng phó biến đổi khí hậu vào vị trí trung tm trong phát triển kinh tế - xã hội |
| Linh hoạt chuyển đổi, thích ứng biến đổi khí hậu |
| Phát huy vai trò nông dn trong bảo vệ môi trường, thích ứng biến đổi khí hậu |

items.title: Tăng cường khả năng chống chịu biến đổi khí hậu của đô thị
items.summary: Để hiện thực hóa mục tiêu này, ông Luigi Cipolla đề xuất áp dụng Phương pháp Quy hoạch thông minh tích hợp (Integrated Smart Planning). Phương pháp này ứng dụng công nghệ GIS, dữ liệu vệ tinh đa thời gian và trí tuệ nhn tạo (AI) để phn tích diễn biến biến đổi khí hậu, từ đó xác định chính xác các "điểm nóng" bị tổn thương cao nhất để ưu tiên phn bổ nguồn vốn đầu tư hạ tầng xanh - lam và giải pháp dựa vào tự nhiên (NBS).

items.title: Biến đổi khí hậu khốc liệt, các nước đang phát triển cần hàng trăm tỷ USD để ứng phó
items.summary:
Các khoản viện trợ hoặc đầu tư nhằm hỗ trợ các nước thích ứng với tình trạng biến đổi khí hậu dự kiến tiếp tục là chủ đề nóng tại Hội nghị lần thứ 31 các bên tham gia Công ước khung của Liên hợp quốc về biến đổi khí hậu (COP31), nơi các nhà đàm phán đến từ gần 200 quốc gia và vùng lãnh thổ sẽ nhóm họp tại TP.Antalya của Thổ Nhĩ Kỳ từ ngày 9 - 20/11. Theo ông Antonio Guterres - Tổng thư ký Liên hợp quốc nhấn mạnh trong bối cảnh đó, báo cáo đã chỉ ra tình trạng thiếu hụt nghiêm trọng khi mỗi USD [...] 11:00 07/11/2026

  Biến đổi khí hậu không còn là cu chuyện của tương lai mà đang hiện hữu qua những đợt nắng nóng kéo dài, mưa lớn bất thường, rét trái mùa và tình trạng ngập úng ngày càng khó lường. Những biến động này không chỉ gy thiệt hại về kinh tế, môi trường mà còn đặt ra những nguy cơ trực tiếp đối với sức khỏe và tính mạng con người.

  Góc nhìn tuần qua
 Biến đổi khí hậu khốc liệt, các nước đang phát triển cần hàng trăm tỷ USD để ứng phó [...] Cùng với dự báo hiện tượng El Nino hoạt động mạnh bất thường trong năm nay sẽ tiếp tục kéo theo các hình thái thời tiết cực đoan, IFRC cảnh báo việc đầu tư vào công tác ứng phó và thích ứng đang ngày càng trở nên cấp thiết. IFRC cũng chỉ ra rằng biến đổi khí hậu đang gy ra các đợt nắng nóng gay gắt, bão lũ và hạn hán khắc nghiệt, đe dọa trực tiếp đến tính mạng, sinh kế và sức khỏe của con người trong thời gian tới.
